name: Tresillo
description: Tresillo (also Rocambor) is a historic Spanish trick-taking game for three players. It is the Spanish descendant of L'Hombre (Ombre), which was once the most popular card game in Europe. The 'declarer' (El Hombre) plays alone against the other two. Uses a 40-card Spanish deck with the unusual A-3-K ranking.

history.origins: Descended from Ombre/L'Hombre, the dominant European card game of the 17th-18th centuries.
timeline: Present: Still played in some regions.
history.cultural: Historically significant as the ancestor of many modern trick-taking games.
history.evolution: Simplified from Ombre while retaining the Matadors (Spadille, Manille, Basto).

setup.deck: 40-card Spanish deck. Rank varies by suit (Long vs Round). Matadors: Spadille (Aâ™ ), Manille (7/2 of trumps), Basto (Aâ™£) are always top trumps.
setup.dealing: Deal 9 cards each. 13 remain in stock.

rules.objective: Declarer must win more tricks than either opponent.
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal 9. 2. Bid (Normal, Vuelta, Solo). Highest bid becomes Declarer. 3. Declarer discards and draws from stock. Opponents may also draw. 4. Play 9 tricks. Follow suit. Trumps beat plain. 5. Declarer wins if taking 5+ tricks (against 2 opponents).

strategy.basic: Bid with strong trump holdings. Matadors are essential.
strategy.intermediate: Exchange to void a suit for trumping.
strategy.advanced: Count opponents' possible holdings. Manage the Matadors.
tips: Spadille (Aâ™ ) is always the highest trump.
